explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The statement is built from the library's own notions: `Place`, `IsCurveOver` (a class in Definitions/Def_AlgebraicCurve_IsCurveOver.lean) and `Place.IsRational` (defined in Definitions/Def_AlgebraicCurve_PlaceEvaluation.lean as surjectivity of `algebraMap K v.ResidueField`). Mathlib has no counterpart to any of these. The one Mathlib ingredient is `IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral` (an integral algebra over an algebraically closed field has a bijective algebra map). That lemma can only be applied after the library's own fact `IsCurveOver.finiteResidue` shows the residue field is finite-dimensional over K. So the derivation needs a library lemma as an auxiliary step. It is not a plain instantiation of a single Mathlib declaration, and the result's specific content (every place of a curve over an algebraically closed field is rational) lies in the library's definitions.
